subject: Problems with compiling R-INLA on linux system

messages.author: fe7c605d4ef9a9e4
messages.subject: Problems with compiling R-INLA on linux system
parts:
Hi

Our sys-admin tried to compile the R-INLA for use on our linux cluster. Unfortunately the version of the OS is pretty old with an old RHEL5 X11 and to compile the fmesher a number of newer X11 libs are needed, and those cannot work together with our current X11 setup.

Sysadmin is reluctant to update the X11 installation for various reasons, Firstly, we have a stabil system right that works well in every other aspects. Secondly, updating X11 is a huge task and we risk ending up having an unstable system. Thirdly, the current cluster will be fased out within the next few months in favour of a new cluster with a more recent version of OS.

Is it possible to compile the fmesher disabling the dependency on X11. I can see that there is a compiler directive FMESHER_NO_X. Setting this to false will that solve our problems?

Thank you for INLA and thanks for any ideas on how to solve this.

Yours sincerely

Frede Aakmann Tøgersen

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problems with compiling R-INLA on linux system
parts:
On 19/09/14 08:34, INLA help wrote:
> On Fri, 2014-09-19 at 00:31 -0700, Frede Tøgersen wrote:
>
>> Is it possible to compile the fmesher disabling the dependency on X11.
>> I can see that there is a compiler directive FMESHER_NO_X. Setting
>> this to false will that solve our problems?
>
> yes, that would do.

It actually needs to be set to true/non-zero, e.g. FMESHER_NO_X=1, but
yes, that directive is there for this reason.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problems with compiling R-INLA on linux system
parts:
On 19/09/14 08:31, Frede Tøgersen wrote:
> Is it possible to compile the fmesher disabling the dependency on X11. I
> can see that there is a compiler directive FMESHER_NO_X. Setting this to
> false will that solve our problems?

You also need to change OS_LDFLAGS so it doesn't include "-lX11".

Finn
